subject: Per-tenant cost-cap + on-demand residency for Halebridge pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@halebridge.com>

Subject: Per-tenant cost-cap + on-demand residency for Halebridge pilot

Team —

Quick context: Halebridge (large regional bank) is ready to sign a 6‑month pilot with a path to enterprise in Q4. Procurement signed off on commercial terms contingent on two guarantees: a per-tenant monthly spend cap to control P&L during the pilot, and an ability to spin up a dedicated residency (residency=model affinity/warm pool for their tenant) on demand for high-load days. They want these in the SOW by 6/30 to get internal approvals.

High level asks:
- Per-tenant monthly cost cap: when the tenant hits X USD in a month, requests should either throttle with a configurable 429 response or route to a fallback, configurable cheaper model.
- On‑demand residency: ability to request a short‑lived residency slot (24–72h) that pins a small warm pool and KV cache for their tenant to avoid cold-start P95 spike during their marketing pushes.

Why this matters:
- Pilot value: ~$75k ARR if converted; large reference opportunity in our banking vertical.
- Risk tolerance: Halebridge needs contractual language; procurement wants an engineering-backed feasibility note.

Asks for Product/Eng:
1) Feasibility and high-level implementation approach (routing/traffic shaping, token accounting, cache partitioning).
2) Rough engineering effort and earliest safe ETA for a gated pilot (we're okay with an MVP that requires manual enablement and an operational playbook).
3) Any non-obvious security/compliance blockers (KMS, tenant data residency, audit trails).

Attached: SOW draft and requirements matrix from customer.

Desired next step: short sync tomorrow or a quick async note with feasibility + one slide theatre for procurement.

Thanks —
Soojin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-tenant cost-cap + on-demand residency for Halebridge pilot

Thanks for the concise write-up, Soojin — helpful. Quick thoughts / clarifying Qs before we scope: 

1) Cost cap semantics: do they want an absolute hard cap that rejects requests at the gateway once reached, or a soft cap that alerts + routes to a cheaper model after a threshold? Procurement language usually wants "hard" guarantees, but those imply customer-visible failures we should discuss.

2) Residency trigger: is this a manual API call from their SRE/provisioning team (preferred for MVP) or should it be automatic based on metrics (traffic spike detection)?

3) Fallback model: do they accept a smaller quantized variant of the same model, or would they prefer a different architecture (e.g., smaller LLM with deterministic guards)?

Operational constraints I want engineering to consider: isolation of KV caches (per-tenant), accounting and billing hooks (token-metering by tenant across fallbacks), and rolling back residency if we observe resource contention.

Marcus — can you weigh in with a high-level implementation approach and a rough T-shirt estimate (S/M/L) for an MVP (manual enable + documented runbook)? If we can do a manual residency enable with routing rules and a fallback by mid‑July we may keep the pilot on track.

If helpful, I'm happy to run a 30‑min triage with Halebridge procurement + their infra lead.

—Jordan
Product Manager, Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@halebridge.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-tenant cost-cap + on-demand residency for Halebridge pilot

Looping in eng POV. TL;DR: feasible as an MVP with manual controls; estimated 3–4 sprints of scoped work to get a robust, automatable flow.

Implementation sketch (MVP):
- Cost cap: implement per-tenant token meter that updates in near-real time (uses existing metering stream). Add a policy engine check at the routing layer that compares tenant spend to configured monthly cap. Policy action options: respond 429, route to fallback model, or switch to degraded throughput. For contractual "hard cap" we can implement 429 but need explicit customer sign-off on user experience.
- Residency bucket (on-demand): create a reservation API (internal) that pins a small warm pool (N GPUs shared across tenants via soft-affinity) and enables a tenant-scoped KV cache namespace. This will be manual-first: CS/Eng ops call internal API to spin reservation.
- Fallback: support routing to a smaller quantized model in the same compute pool; cost and quality delta documented.

Engineering effort (rough):
- Policy/routing check + token-meter integration: 1–2 sprints (backend + gateway).
- Reservation API + warm pool wiring + KV namespace partitioning: 2 sprints (ops + runtime).
- Testing, docs, and runbook + small UI/console flag: 1 sprint.
Total: ~4 sprints (8 weeks) for an end-to-end automated experience. For a manual MVP we can cut to ~2 sprints (~4 weeks) by deferring console work and using an ops-only reservation flow.

Risks / blockers:
- Billing accuracy: we must ensure token accounting across fallback routes is tied to the tenant for the cap. That involves small changes to the metering pipeline (coord with Billing team).
- Resource contention: soft-affinity for warm pools means noisy neighbors risk; for pilot we can contain this by reserving a small dedicated warm pool per Halebridge during their reservation window. That increases cost exposure and should be reflected in the SOW.
- Security/KMS: if residency implies caching customer prompts, confirm retention and encryption requirements. If they require customer-managed CMK we need legal + infra sign-off (timeline + ops complexity).

Recommendation: Offer them an "MVP manual residency + soft cap with fallback routing" option in the SOW. We provide an operational playbook (manual enable, monitoring checklist, clear fallbacks) and a clause that a hard rejection behavior (429) is available but will be treated as a last resort and requires explicit acceptance.

Will align with Billing and Security tomorrow and can produce a one‑pager for procurement.

—Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Marcus, please do the one‑pager (feasibility + recommended MVP path + estimate) by EOD Friday so I can attach it to the SOW. Call out explicitly: manual enable flow, fallback to quantized model, and the cost delta for reserving a small warm pool.
2) Jordan/Marissa — can you confirm the CS/ops playbook owner (who runs the manual reservation) and what SLA we can promise for a reservation turnaround (we suggested <4h in commercial talk track).
3) Elena — procurement asked for sample contract language that describes the cap behavior. For the MVP we're proposing: "soft cap with automatic fallback + ops escalation to pause traffic". If Halebridge requires hard reject we will include it as a negotiable term with a specific sea‑change on the pilot acceptance criteria.

If everyone is aligned I'll schedule a 30-min triage with Halebridge procurement + our Billing/Security leads tomorrow.

Soojin
